pages.title: What is Inheritance
pages.content: Inheritance allows a subclass to reuse members of a superclass with the `extends` keyword. A subclass can directly use inherited methods and add its own behavior.

callout.title: Key takeaway
callout.text: Inheritance lets a subclass reuse and extend superclass behavior.

checkpoint.question: Which feature allows a subclass to provide its own implementation of an inherited method?
checkpoint.explanation: Method overriding lets a subclass redefine an inherited instance method.

pages.title: What is Polymorphism
pages.content: Polymorphism allows a superclass reference to refer to a subclass object. With method overriding, the subclass implementation is selected at runtime.

callout.title: Key takeaway
callout.text: Overridden methods enable runtime polymorphism.

questions.question: What is a class?
options: A blueprint defining object state and behavior
questions.explanation: A class defines fields and methods used by its objects.

questions.question: What does `new` do when creating an object?
options: Creates an object and invokes a constructor
questions.explanation: `new` allocates an object and invokes a constructor.

questions.question: Where are instance fields stored conceptually?
options: Only in static memory shared by all objects
questions.explanation: Each object has its own instance-field state.

questions.question: What is a method?
options: A named block of behavior that can be invoked
questions.explanation: Methods encapsulate reusable behavior.

questions.question: What is method overloading?
options: Same method name with different parameter lists
Same method body in two files
Changing a field type at runtime
Calling a constructor from another class only
questions.explanation: Overloads differ by parameter list and are resolved at compile time.

questions.question: What is a constructor used for?
options: Returning a value from a method
questions.explanation: Constructors initialize objects when they are created.

questions.question: What is constructor overloading?
options: Multiple constructors with different parameter lists
Using multiple classes with one object
questions.explanation: Constructors can be overloaded by parameter list.

questions.question: Which keyword establishes class inheritance?
questions.explanation: `extends` creates a subclass relationship.

questions.question: What is runtime polymorphism in Java?
options: A superclass reference invoking an overridden subclass method
Calling an overloaded method at compile time
questions.explanation: Dynamic dispatch selects the overridden method for the actual object.

questions.question: Which is compile-time polymorphism?
questions.explanation: Overload resolution occurs at compile time.

questions.question: Which keyword begins a block that may throw an exception?
questions.explanation: The risky operation is placed in a try block.

questions.question: Which block handles a matching exception?
questions.explanation: A catch block handles an exception of a compatible type.

questions.question: When does `finally` normally execute?
options: After try/catch whether or not an exception occurs
questions.explanation: Finally is intended for cleanup that should occur regardless of normal/exceptional completion.

questions.question: What exception can `10 / 0` cause for integers?
questions.explanation: Integer division by zero throws ArithmeticException.

questions.question: What exception can `Integer.parseInt("abc")` cause?
questions.explanation: Invalid numeric text causes NumberFormatException.

questions.question: What exception can an invalid array index cause?
questions.explanation: Accessing outside an array's valid index range throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

questions.question: Why use multiple catch blocks?
options: To handle different exception types differently
To run all catches for one exception
questions.explanation: Each matching catch can provide type-specific handling.

questions.question: What should a custom exception name communicate?
questions.explanation: Descriptive names make the failure domain clear.

questions.question: Which statement about checked custom exceptions is correct?
options: A class can extend Exception and must be handled or declared
questions.explanation: Checked exceptions extending Exception are subject to Java's checked-exception rules.

questions.question: What is a good reason to use a custom exception?
options: To make domain validation failures explicit
To replace ordinary if statements everywhere
To force all methods to throw
questions.explanation: Custom exceptions are useful for meaningful domain-specific failure conditions.

questions.question: What is implicit widening conversion?
options: Assigning a smaller compatible primitive type to a larger one
questions.explanation: Java performs several widening primitive conversions automatically.

questions.question: Which is a widening conversion?
questions.explanation: int to double is a widening primitive conversion.

questions.question: What can happen during narrowing conversion?
options: The program automatically sorts the value
questions.explanation: Narrowing may truncate or overflow depending on the conversion.

questions.question: How do you explicitly narrow a double to int?
questions.explanation: A cast is required for narrowing a double to int.

questions.question: What is precision loss?
options: Some significant information is not preserved in a conversion
questions.explanation: Converting to a lower-precision representation can lose detail.

questions.question: What is a reference type?
options: A variable that holds a reference to an object
questions.explanation: Reference variables hold references to objects.

questions.question: What is upcasting?
options: Assigning a subclass object to a superclass reference
questions.explanation: Upcasting to a superclass is a safe widening reference conversion.

questions.question: What is downcasting?
options: Casting a superclass reference to a more specific subclass type
questions.explanation: Downcasting narrows a reference to a subclass type and must be type-safe.

questions.question: Which operator safely checks an object's runtime type before a cast?
questions.explanation: `instanceof` tests whether an object is compatible with a given reference type.

questions.question: What should you consider before downcasting?
options: Whether the referenced object is actually an instance of the target subtype
questions.explanation: A downcast is valid only when the object has the target runtime type.
